sections.html:
Polk County is Iowa's most populous county, with 492,401 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 516,546 in 2025. Des Moines is the county seat, the state capital and the largest city in Iowa.

The county covers about 591.9 square miles, roughly 19.2 of them water, and the Des Moines River runs through the middle of it. It was created on January 13, 1846 and organized on March 1, 1846, and it is named for President James K. Polk. The present courthouse was built in 1906 and renovated and enlarged in 1962.

sections.h2: What drives the Polk County economy?
sections.html:
The Des Moines area is a major U.S. insurance and finance center, and that sector is the core of the Polk County job base. Principal Financial Group and Wellmark Blue Cross Blue Shield are headquartered in Des Moines, and Wells Fargo, Voya and Nationwide have large operations nearby.

The six-county Des Moines metro held 779,048 people in 2024, the largest metro located entirely in Iowa, per Wikipedia's Des Moines article. Data centers run by Microsoft, Hewlett-Packard and others also operate in the area.

sections.h2: How do the cities and suburbs in Polk County differ for a seller?
sections.html:
Polk County mixes one large city with a ring of suburbs, and each is its own tax and school setting. Besides Des Moines, the metro includes West Des Moines, Urbandale, Windsor Heights, Clive, Ankeny, Johnston, Waukee and Altoona.

  • Des Moines Independent Community School District is the largest in Iowa, with 63 schools.
  • Parts of Des Moines south of County Line Road extend into Warren County, so a Des Moines address can be taxed by a different county.
  • Neighborhoods named in the city's profile include downtown, the East Village and South of Grand.

Check which county's treasurer bills a parcel before you ask for a payoff. A mailing address says little about it.

sections.h2: How do people get around Polk County?
sections.html:
Interstate 235 runs through Des Moines, while I-35 and I-80 pass through the metro and share a stretch on the north side. The Des Moines Bypass runs south and east of the city.

DART operates the public bus system for the city and its suburbs, and Des Moines International Airport offers domestic nonstop service. Fort Des Moines was established in 1843 where the Des Moines and Raccoon rivers meet, and the city was incorporated in 1851. The county's median household income was $82,405 in the figures Wikipedia reports, which a seller can use as rough context but not as a pricing guide.

sections.h2: What flood and weather history should Polk County owners know?
sections.html:
The Des Moines and Raccoon rivers meet downtown, and major floods hit in 1993 and 2008. In 1993 the Des Moines Water Works flooded and about 250,000 people lost running water for 12 days, and in 2008 a levee breach caused serious flooding.

Saylorville Reservoir upstream controls the Des Moines River, but it overtopped its spillway in both of those years. The Flood of 1851 had destroyed much of the early town.

Des Moines has hot, humid summers and cold winters, with average annual precipitation near 36.55 inches and snowfall near 36.5 inches. Frequent afternoon thunderstorms come in spring and summer. A seller near a river should have flood zone and insurance information ready for a buyer.

sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Polk County?
sections.html:
The Polk County Assessor values property and the Polk County Treasurer collects the tax. The Assessor is at 111 Court Avenue, Room 195, Des Moines, IA 50309, phone (515) 286-3014.

The Treasurer's office has been open 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. for all services since June 3, 2024, and the Treasurer's page says payment options are available when the office is closed. The office also administers the Senior and Disabled Property Tax Credit for owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and meet the yearly income limits.

Polk assessments follow the state two-year cycle. Values are updated in odd-numbered years and usually left alone in even-numbered years, apart from new construction, demolition or other property-specific changes, and notices go out before April 1 when a value changes.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Polk County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written, signed protest between April 2 and April 30, using a separate form for each parcel. If April 30 lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day.

  • Owners may ask the Assessor for an informal review from April 2 through April 25.
  • A signed agreement with the Assessor avoids the formal protest.
  • Evidence helps: an appraisal, recent sales, or three to five comparable sales.
  • Value should reflect the January 1 assessment date.

Forms exist for residential, commercial and agricultural property. The Assessor says commercial owners may offer three years of operating statements and a current rent roll, though that is not required. Grounds follow Iowa Code 441.37, and the details are in the Assessor summary.

sections.h2: What happens at the Polk County board of review?
sections.html:
The board meets in May and usually finishes by May 31, with an oral hearing available if you asked for one at filing. It mails a written decision with its reasons.

You can then appeal to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or go to district court, with 20 days counted from adjournment or May 31, whichever is later. State rules also allow the board to hold an odd-year special session from October 10 to November 15, and its only ground is that a state equalization order would raise the value above actual value, per the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: When is Polk County property tax delinquent, and what is the tax sale?
sections.html:
Under Iowa law the first half is delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1, and interest is one and one-half percent a month, rounded to the nearest dollar with a $1 floor (Iowa Code 445.39). Confirm your own due dates with the Treasurer, because the county's pages list payment dates in more than one way.

Delinquent parcels go to the annual sale on the third Monday in June by default. Polk's 2024 sale was held on June 17, 2024 with online bidding, and the property list ran in the Altoona Herald on June 5, 2024. Owners can redeem by paying the sale price, fees and 2% monthly interest from the month of sale (Iowa Code 447.1).

sections.h2: How does tax get handled when a Polk County house sells?
sections.html:
The deed carries a declaration of value to the recorder, who passes it to the assessor, and transfer tax is 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). The statute does not say which side pays, so the contract does.

Property tax is a lien on the parcel against every person except the state. For the homestead credit, a buyer of a house sold before July 1 must file by July 1, while a sale on or after July 1 keeps the credit with the property that year, according to rule 701-110.1.

  • Order a payoff from the Treasurer for each parcel.
  • Confirm which county bills a parcel near County Line Road.
  • Ask the closing agent who covers the second-half tax and transfer tax.

faqs.q: What is the Polk County Assessor's address?
faqs.a: 111 Court Avenue, Room 195, Des Moines, IA 50309. The phone number is (515) 286-3014.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Polk County property tax assessment?
faqs.a: From April 2 through April 30. A separate signed form is needed for each parcel, and a weekend deadline moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: How often are Polk County values updated?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years, with few changes in even years beyond new construction, demolition or property-specific changes.

faqs.q: Can part of Des Moines be taxed by Warren County?
faqs.a: Yes. Parts of Des Moines south of County Line Road extend into Warren County, so ask which county's treasurer bills your parcel.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Iowa property tax?
faqs.a: One and one-half percent per month, rounded to the nearest whole dollar with a $1 minimum. A fraction of a month counts as a full month.
